why: I compared each verifier check's PASS/FAIL conditions with the words of its expect line. Check 1 requires only `exit 1` and empty stdout. Check 2 requires `bad config:`, the exact path, and line 3 and column 3 "in any clear form", so it demands no exact wording. Check 3 requires only `OK`, meaning the call threw and the message contains the path. Check 4 requires `listening on 9000`, exit 0 and a deepEqual to `{ port: 9000 }`. Check 5 requires that `npm test` passes, that a test checking the path exists, and that this test fails against the base `src/`. That last condition just restates "fails at the current base commit". The stricter items from the proofs all sit under "Advisory (not pass/fail)", not in any PASS or FAIL condition: whether the location depends on Node's own message, ENOENT behaviour, absolute-path resolution and README changes. None of the conditions goes beyond what its expect line says.
